chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Asbahani, from al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever seeks hadith for the benefit of this world, there will be no share for him in the Hereafter.

key_terms.الآخرة: The Hereafter — the realm of the afterlife, the ultimate abode of reward and reckoning
key_terms.الحديث: Hadith — prophetic narration/tradition; here used as a metonym for religious knowledge and its study
key_terms.منفعة الدنيا: Benefit of this world — worldly gain, material advantage, or social prestige
key_terms.نصيب: Share/portion — one's allotted reward or lot in the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about seeking hadith for worldly benefit?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns that seeking religious knowledge (hadith) with a worldly motive — for personal gain, status, or profit — nullifies any spiritual reward in the Hereafter. This teaching addresses the dangerous corruption of sincere intent (niyyah), which is foundational in Islamic ethics. The early Muslim community was acutely aware that the transmission of hadith could be exploited for worldly advancement, and this saying serves as a stern reminder that the inward motivation determines one's ultimate standing before God.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad Al Asbahany, from Al Minqary, from Hafs Bin Giyas, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who intends (acquiring) the Hadeeth for the benefit of the world, there would not happen to be for him a share in the Hereafter’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isbahani from al-Minqari from Hafs ibn Ghiyath from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“Whoever would want al-Hadith for the worldly gains he will have no share for it in the next life.”
